Use a finite-volume grid on x in [-1,1] with Nx=400 cells, dx=0.005, and cell centers x_j=-1+(j+0.5)*dx for j=0,...,399.
Use periodic boundary conditions by wrapping ghost-cell indices.
Set Gamma=1.6666666666666667, eta=0.1, zeta=0.1, T=0.5, and CFL=0.4.
Set initial cell-averaged primitive variables rho_j=1.0+0.2*sin(pi*x_j), v_j=0.1*cos(pi*x_j), and p_j=1.0+0.2*cos(pi*x_j).
Initialize conservative variables as m_j=rho_j*v_j and E_j=p_j/(Gamma-1)+0.5*rho_j*v_j^2.
Evolve the conservative variables U=[rho,m,E] using the semi-discrete finite-volume system dU_j/dt=-(F_{j+1/2}-F_{j-1/2})/dx.
Compute the inviscid Rusanov flux at each interface using F_conv=[m, m^2/rho+p, (E+p)*v] with v=m/rho.
Use the interface wave speed a=max(|v_L|+c_L, |v_R|+c_R) with c=sqrt(Gamma*p/rho).
Compute the Rusanov flux as F_hat=0.5*(F_conv(U_L)+F_conv(U_R))-0.5*a*(U_R-U_L).
Compute cell-centered v_x_j=(v_{j+1}-v_{j-1})/(2*dx) with periodic wrap.
Compute sigma_j=(zeta+4/3*eta)*v_x_j at cell centers.
At each interface, set sigma_face=0.5*(sigma_j+sigma_{j+1}) and v_face=0.5*(v_j+v_{j+1}) with periodic wrap.
Set the viscous flux contribution as F_visc=[0, -sigma_face, -v_face*sigma_face].
Use the total interface flux F_total=F_hat+F_visc.
Enforce positivity by clipping rho and p to a small floor of 1e-12 if needed, where p is recovered from p=(Gamma-1)*(E-0.5*m^2/rho).
Use SSP-RK2 time integration with U1=U^n+dt*L(U^n) and U^{n+1}=0.5*U^n+0.5*U1+0.5*dt*L(U1).
Choose dt each step as dt=min(dt_conv, dt_visc), with dt_conv=CFL*dx/max_j(|v_j|+c_j) and dt_visc=0.5*dx^2/max(zeta+4/3*eta,1e-30).
Adjust the final time step so that the simulation reaches exactly T=0.5.
At the final time, compute and output rho, v, and p at the cell centers.
Save the file solution_pdebench_cns1d_eta0p1_periodic_smooth.npz containing arrays x, rho, v, p and scalars Gamma, eta, zeta, T, dx, CFL.
Save a 3-panel line plot of rho, v, and p versus x at time T as solution_pdebench_cns1d_eta0p1_periodic_smooth.png.
Print the minimum and maximum of rho and p, and print the mean of rho over the spatial domain.
